llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed CellCog integration, but it is broad enough to expose local files, real browser profiles, connected SaaS tools, and background/long-running agent workflows without tight invocation boundaries.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks agents to use an external service with local file uploads, automatic file downloads, real browser profile access, and connected SaaS integrations; these are high-impact capabilities and are only partially constrained by examples and warnings.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a Markdown skill that instructs users to install the official CellCog Python SDK with pip and set CELLCOG_API_KEY; no bundled executable code or remote code execution payload was found in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest description is very broad, while runtime examples include uploading local files, enabling a real Chrome profile, and enabling connected SaaS tools, including an option that omits tool selection and therefore may allow all connected tools.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents persistent-machine workflows, background notification delivery, default downloads under ~/.cellcog, deterministic writes via GENERATE_FILE, and AI employees with memory and long-running behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capabilities mostly fit the stated purpose of delegating multimodal work to CellCog, including file inputs, generated files, research, browser use, and connected tools.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to delegate work to CellCog. Treat SHOW_FILE paths as uploads to an external service, avoid secrets and private directories, use narrow tools_selection values instead of enabling all SaaS tools, be careful with real Chrome profiles, and prefer task-specific output folders for generated files.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The referenced evidence is API key setup via an environment variable and a CellCog profile link, not access to SSH keys or credential files; this is expected authentication for the service.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad description is supported by the artifact and is material because it is paired with file upload, browser profile, SaaS tool, and background-agent capabilities.
[RA2] expected: File persistence and background continuation are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but they increase impact because outputs can be written to user-specified paths or ~/.cellcog and chats may continue server-side.
[SQP-2] expected: The artifact discloses SHOW_FILE upload and automatic downloads, and includes an earlier warning about sensitive files; however the Working with Files section itself does not require explicit consent or safe output directories.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The supplied SARIF scan reported no results; artifact review still found review-worthy overbreadth in optional high-impact integrations.
